kind = "proof"

*Step 1.* Suppose $\mathcal G|_U$ is generated by $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal G(U)$, i.e. the morphism $\pi:\underline{\Lambda^n}_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ sending the $j$-th basis vector to $s_j$ is an epimorphism of sheaves on the localized site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. An epimorphism of sheaves is locally surjective, and the sheafification map of the constant presheaf with value $\Lambda^n$ is locally surjective; so their composite, the presheaf map $\Lambda^n\to\mathcal G(-)$, is locally surjective.

*Step 2.* Let $z\in\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], represented by a section $t$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$. By cofilteredness there is a pointed neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ mapping to both $(V,\bar v)$ and $(U,\bar u)$. By Step 1 there are a further pointed refinement $R\to W$ and $c\in\Lambda^n$ whose image in $\mathcal G(R)$ is $t|_R$. Since the source presheaf is constant, this image is the restriction of the section $\sum_jc_js_j\in\mathcal G(U)$. Taking germs, $z$ is the germ at $(U,\bar u)$ of $\sum_jc_js_j$, so the germs of $s_1,\dots,s_n$ span $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ (also for $n=0$).

*Step 3.* Since $\mathcal G$ is of finite type, there is an etale covering of $Y$ on each member of which $\mathcal G$ is generated by finitely many sections. Choose a member $U$ whose image contains the image point of $\bar y$; as $\Omega$ is separably closed, $\bar y$ lifts to a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$. Step 2 shows that $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is finitely generated.
